Fetal Echo Project · Unit D13 · Detect tier · v0.1

Quality assurance and audit

DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

You will be able to

  • Name the four things by which the quality of a screening examination is judged.
  • Say what should be stored from every cardiac screen, and why.
  • Set up a simple audit of your own images and detection.
  • Use a checklist for the five planes on every patient.

What quality means

The quality of a screening examination is judged on four things: image quality, acquisition of the standard planes, appropriate interpretation of the views, and complete documentation.1

The 2023 guideline added sections on quality assurance and on the use of a checklist.2

Why it matters

In one retrospective study of missed diagnoses, failure to meet technical criteria contributed to about half of the misses. Failure to recognise abnormal anatomy on an adequate view accounted for nearly a third more.3

Image quality starts with set-up

Use settings that favour a high frame rate with more contrast and high resolution: low persistence, a single focal zone and a fairly narrow image field. Cardiac presets usually include these.4

Magnify until the heart fills at least a third to a half of the screen.5

What to store

Still frames and video clips of the recommended structures and views should be archived, so that the examination can be reviewed later for adequacy. Identify the patient appropriately in the clinical record, label laterality and orientation where appropriate, and take local or national archiving standards into account.6

The views of the right ventricular outflow tract, the branch pulmonary arteries and the two arches form a continuum. They are likely to be judged more reliably live or on a clip than from still images alone.7

For a full fetal echocardiogram, the echocardiography guideline asks for stills, moving clips and a structured report. It requires a sweep from the stomach to the upper mediastinum, and two-dimensional and colour clips of the individual views, including the three-vessel view and the three-vessel-and-trachea view.8

The same guideline says images should be kept in a secure digital archive that allows retrieval for review, that local legal requirements decide how long they are kept, and that a study which stays non-diagnostic after optimisation should have its limitations stated in the report.9,10,11

Auditing yourself

Audit of stored stills or clips against quality criteria set in advance is encouraged.12

Each practice is encouraged to review its own detection rates and diagnostic accuracy every year, and to arrange further training where the review shows a need.12

Continuous training based on feedback, standardised protocols, a low threshold for referral and easy access to fetal heart specialists can all improve a programme. For fetal echocardiography services, ongoing quality improvement should be documented.13,14

How a practice samples its studies and scores them is a local decision. The guideline gives no method, and none is taught here; see the missing claims for this unit.

The checklist

The checklist below gathers the main criteria for the five planes, for learning and for audit. It is a selection. Completing it does not by itself establish a complete normal examination.

Five-plane screening checklist (main criteria)

  • Fetal left and right worked out first15
  • Upper abdomen at the abdominal circumference level: stomach on the left; descending aorta left of the spine; inferior vena cava right of the spine16
  • Heart mainly in the left chest; usually no larger than a third of the chest area17,18
  • Axis about 45 degrees to the left (plus or minus 20) of the front-to-back axis of the chest18
  • Rate 120 to 160 per minute, regular19
  • Atria similar in size; foramen ovale flap moving within the left atrium; septum primum present20
  • At least one pulmonary vein seen entering the left atrium on grey-scale, where technically feasible21
  • Ventricles similar in size, walls not thick; moderator band near the apex marks the right ventricle. Asymmetry in mid-gestation needs further examination; mild disproportion can be a third-trimester variant22,23
  • Ventricular septum examined from apex to crux, with the adequacy of the view recorded24,25
  • Two atrioventricular valves opening separately and freely; septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve inserted nearer the apex26
  • LVOT: vessel from the left ventricle, anterior wall continuous with the septum, not dividing; valve not thickened, moving freely27,28,29
  • RVOT: vessel from the right ventricle, dividing after a short course; valve not thickened, moving freely27,30
  • Great arteries cross and are approximately equal in size31,27
  • Three-vessel view: number, size, alignment and arrangement of the three vessels32
  • Three-vessel-and-trachea view: V shape, both arches left of the trachea, arches similar in size33,34
  • Stills and clips of the recommended views stored; laterality and orientation labelled where appropriate6

Still to be written

  • A scoring system for image quality of each cardiac plane (published criteria with points) - needs a source.
  • A target or benchmark detection rate to audit against - needs a source; none is stated in the guideline claims held.
  • How long images must be kept and how PC-PNDT record-keeping applies to stored clips in India - the echocardiography guideline only says to follow local legal requirements (AS23-114); needs an Indian legal source and the advisor's input.
  • A method for sampling studies, scoring them and working out a practice's own detection rate and accuracy - not given in the guideline; needs a source or the editor's design.
  • How to obtain outcome feedback after delivery in Indian practice - needs the editor's input.
